issues_confirmed.summary: Scraper targets the legacy Places API, which Google closed to new customers on 2025-03-01, while the setup flow instructs clients to create a new Cloud project and enable it. Blocks onboarding any new client and blocks key/project rotation; today's build works only because it rides one grandfathered project.

issues_confirmed.summary: billing_guard hardcodes 10,000 free calls/month per endpoint and tells the client it is 'Stopping to avoid charges', but that figure matches neither Google pricing model (legacy = one shared $200 monthly credit across SKUs; post-2025 = per-SKU Essentials/Pro/Enterprise caps, all below 10,000 for these SKUs). The guard lets the client run past the free allowance onto their card. Counter also increments before the HTTP request, so timeouts burn budget.

issues_confirmed.summary: _sent_today() compares local midnight against naive-UTC created_at rows, so between 00:00 and 05:00 PKT it returns 0 regardless of how much was just sent - both the pre-flight check and the in-loop re-check are bypassed. Separately, cli.py send has no cap at all, only throttle pacing, and README.md:34 points the client at that path.

issues_confirmed.summary: Legacy Places returns HTTP 200 for REQUEST_DENIED / OVER_QUERY_LIMIT / INVALID_REQUEST with the error in the JSON status field, but only raise_for_status() is called. A denied key yields results=[], saved stays 0, mark_done still runs, and is_done then skips the area for 30 days. Also silently truncates pagination at 20 results.

issues_confirmed.note: Migrating to Places API (New) fixes this for free - the new API returns real 4xx codes, so raise_for_status starts working. Folded into TODO task 2.

browser_note: Not run. standalone/ has no .venv, no installed deps, no config.ini and no supplier_scraper.db, and _setup_guard (web_server.py:66-70) redirects every route to /setup until config.ini exists - creating one would mean writing a project config file, which this review is not allowed to do. More to the point, the headline finding is specific to the frozen PyInstaller build (Path(sys.executable).parent), which a source run cannot reproduce: in dev the __file__ fallback at cli.py:25 / web_server.py:630 finds cities_us.txt and everything looks fine. Verified by reading all five frozen/dev path resolution sites instead.

proposed_tasks.title: Ship cities_us.txt in the release zip (plus a _MEIPASS fallback and a CI assertion)
Migrate the two Places call sites to Places API (New) behind an adapter - also fixes the silent REQUEST_DENIED bug
One shared daily send cap for both send paths, compared in a single consistent timezone
Drop 'rating' from DETAILS_FIELDS and replace billing_guard's fictional free-tier numbers with the real ones
Fix the wrong Gist manifest filename in README.md (3 places) before it re-breaks the update banner

verdict: Solid, well-factored little product that works from source and is quietly broken where it counts: the shipped exe cannot do its headline --all-us scrape, and the scraper is built on a Google API no new client can enable. Four months idle with three untouched TODO lists - the code is not the bottleneck, the decision to pick it up or formally park it is.
